category_title: Students with disabilities who do not respond to teacher questions or volunteer for individual performances
minimal_context: The teacher is asking fourth-grade students in the inclusive music classroom to volunteer to play prepared pieces on their recorders.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to play our prepared pieces on the recorders now. Who would like to volunteer to play first?

STUDENT: (Sits quietly and does not raise his hand to volunteer.)

TUTOR: Raul volunteered, but we need more students. Who else wants to volunteer?

STUDENT: (Looks at the recorder but does not volunteer to play.)

TUTOR: Adam, would you like to volunteer to play your prepared piece?

STUDENT: (Does not volunteer to play the prepared piece and does not respond to the question.)

options.A: Purposefully plan for individual participation opportunities when developing lesson plans and work in collaboration with music therapists and special educators to develop appropriate activities and adaptations.
options.B: Have the student complete reflective journal entries in which he is encouraged to write or draw freely on his experience playing prepared pieces on the recorder.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end of each task when asking students to volunteer to play their prepared pieces on the recorders during the music session.
options.D: Implement a specific 'Termination' stage counting down the final three to five sessions of the music program when asking students to volunteer to play prepared pieces.
